pattern.top_pattern: CA acute hospitals are under both admission and unit-cost pressure
pattern.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual inpatient spend in CA acute hospitals across HMO, EPO, and PPO
key_driver_codes: Chemotherapy without Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis with CC
Major Hematological and Immunological Diagnoses Except Sickle Cell Crisis and Coagulation Disorders with CC
pattern.pattern_details: CA acute hospital spend is rising through a mix of more inpatient activity and higher paid per admit. The largest block is CA HMO acute hospital business, where authorized stays show both higher admissions and materially higher paid per admit, and CA EPO adds another sizable acute utilization increase. Chemotherapy, hematology, back problems, and O'Connor Hospital are recurring contributors inside the broader acute pattern.
pattern.why_it_matters: CA is not just seeing more inpatient use; it is also seeing richer or more expensive acute episodes, which requires joint UM and reimbursement action.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Run a combined CA inpatient action plan: UM should review admission and level-of-care appropriateness, while network and reimbursement teams validate contract performance and case-rate behavior for the acute hospital providers and DRGs showing both volume and unit-cost growth.
evidence_summary: The CA acute hospital pattern totals about $45.3M across HMO, EPO, and PPO.
CA HMO acute hospital authorized stays added about $27.7M with 422 more admissions and about $24.7K higher paid per admit.
CA EPO acute hospital utilization added about $12.9M with 264 more admissions even though paid per admit was slightly down in that segment.
Additional CA acute pressure appears at O'Connor Hospital and in chemotherapy, hematology, and back-problem DRGs.
